questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Message Integrity, Hash Functions, Digital Signatures & HMAC
questions.text: Explain the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability) and the broader security goals (Authentication, Non-repudiation, Access Control). Classify Security Attacks: Passive Attacks (Eavesdropping, Traffic analysis) vs. Active Attacks (Masquerade, Replay, Modification of messages, Denial of Service - DoS/DDoS).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Security Fundamentals, Threat Models & Cryptographic Principles
questions.text: Explain Classical Substitution and Transposition Ciphers: Playfair Cipher, Polyalphabetic (Vigenère) Cipher, Rail Fence Cipher, and Hill Cipher. Encrypt the plaintext message "SECURITY" using a Hill Cipher with key matrix $K = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 4 \\ 5 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \pmod{26}$ and find its decryption matrix $K^{-1}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Security Fundamentals, Threat Models & Cryptographic Principles
questions.text: Explain the structure of Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). Describe the 4 round transformations: (a) `SubBytes` (Non-linear S-Box substitution), (b) `ShiftRows`, (c) `MixColumns` (Matrix multiplication in $GF(2^8)$), and (d) `AddRoundKey` (XOR with round key schedule). Compare AES with DES/3DES.

Explain Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange algorithm. In a Diffie-Hellman setup with public prime $q = 23$ and primitive root $\alpha = 5$, User A selects private key $X_A = 6$ and User B selects $X_B = 15$. (a) Calculate public keys $Y_A$ and $Y_B$, (b) Compute the shared secret session key $K$. Explain Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack on Diffie-Hellman.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Security Fundamentals, Threat Models & Cryptographic Principles
questions.text: What are Cryptographic Hash Functions? Explain the three essential security properties: (a) Pre-image resistance (One-way), (b) Second pre-image resistance (Weak collision resistance), and (c) Collision resistance (Strong collision resistance). Explain the Birthday Attack on hash functions and the structure of SHA-256 / SHA-3.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Public Key Infrastructure, Certificates & Authentication Protocols
questions.text: Explain Digital Signature Scheme (Signing and Verification algorithms) using RSA and Digital Signature Standard (DSS / DSA). Explain Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Digital Certificates (X.509 standard), Certificate Authorities (CA), and Certificate Revocation Lists (CRL).

Explain IPsec Architecture: (a) Authentication Header (AH), (b) Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP), (c) Transport Mode vs. Tunnel Mode, and (d) Security Associations (SA) and Internet Key Exchange (IKE).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Symmetric Key Cryptography & Block Cipher Modes
questions.text: Explain the TLS/HTTPS Handshake Protocol (ClientHello, ServerHello, Certificate verification, Pre-Master Secret exchange, CipherSpec negotiation, and symmetric session key generation). Explain Kerberos Authentication System (Authentication Server - AS and Ticket Granting Server - TGS).

Classify Firewalls: (a) Packet Filtering Firewall (Stateless), (b) Stateful Inspection Firewall, (c) Application-Level Gateway (Proxy), and (d) Circuit-Level Gateway. Explain Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) network design.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Security Fundamentals, Threat Models & Cryptographic Principles
questions.text: Compare Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) vs. Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS). Explain Signature-Based vs. Anomaly-Based detection. Describe common web application vulnerabilities from OWASP Top-10: SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), and Buffer Overflow.
